\subsection{Purpose}




This is the integrated strategy document that connects the previous sections into one coherent operating model.




It does not replace the detailed files. It functions as the final synthesis layer:




\begin{itemize}
\item what the profile is;
\item which roles to target;
\item how to position the portfolio;
\item how to apply;
\item how to negotiate;
\item how to avoid strategic dilution;
\item what to do in the next 90 days;
\item what to build over 12–24 months.
\end{itemize}




This document assumes the thesis is complete and pending defense.




\medskip\hrule\medskip




\section{1. Strategic diagnosis}




\subsection{Current position}




Alexander Woodcock Salomón is best positioned as a \textbf{Real-Time 3D Developer / Unity Technical Artist focused on interactive technical visualization, CAD-to-realtime optimization, Unity WebGL deployment, and Python-assisted tooling}.




The strongest evidence is not formal industry experience. The strongest evidence is the \textbf{TwinSight X500} thesis project, supported by secondary technical projects such as ARA Framework, Blender portrait work, and selected software/tooling experiments.




\subsection{Core asymmetry}




The profile has a strong project but limited formal industry history.




That creates a specific strategy:




\begin{mdcode}
Bloque de codigo: text
Do not compete as a generic junior developer.
Do not compete as a pure 3D artist.
Do not compete as a generic full-stack developer.
Compete as a niche candidate with unusually relevant proof in Unity WebGL, technical visualization and CAD-to-realtime.
\end{mdcode}




\subsection{Main market advantage}




TwinSight creates a defensible bridge between:




\begin{itemize}
\item Unity;
\item WebGL;
\item interactive 3D;
\item CAD-to-realtime asset optimization;
\item technical UI;
\item inspection/assembly visualization;
\item usability validation;
\item technical documentation.
\end{itemize}




This combination is more aligned with \textbf{technical visualization, simulation, digital twins, XR, product visualization and industrial 3D} than with pure game art.




\subsection{Main weakness}




The main weakness is not lack of potential. It is \textbf{lack of packaged proof}.




The profile must be converted into recruiter-readable evidence:




\begin{itemize}
\item case study;
\item demo video;
\item GitHub README;
\item portfolio;
\item screenshots;
\item CV bullets;
\item LinkedIn project entry;
\item interview explanation.
\end{itemize}




Until that exists, the job search will underperform.

\section{7. EU / Portugal / Germany mobility synthesis}




\subsection{Current legal position}




At present, the candidate should say:




\begin{mdcode}
Bloque de codigo: text
I am based in Colombia and available for remote contractor/B2B work. I do not currently hold EU work authorization.
\end{mdcode}




\subsection{Portuguese passport route}




The Portuguese passport expected in \textasciitilde{}2 years is strategically important, but it is not current authorization.




Once issued, it may unlock:




\begin{itemize}
\item right to live and work in Portugal;
\item right to work across EU/EEA subject to local registration rules;
\item easier EU applications;
\item stronger recruiter response for EU roles;
\item relocation without employer-sponsored visa in many cases.
\end{itemize}




Until issued, it should be described carefully:




\begin{mdcode}
Bloque de codigo: text
I expect to obtain Portuguese citizenship/passport in approximately two years, but I am currently Colombia-based and available as a contractor.
\end{mdcode}




\subsection{Germany route through marriage/residence}




Marriage to a German citizen can be a real route if relocation happens legally and the corresponding residence title is granted.




It can potentially unlock:




\begin{itemize}
\item residence in Germany;
\item work authorization;
\item local employment applications;
\item access to German/EU employer market;
\item more relevance for German language.
\end{itemize}




It should not be presented as current work authorization.




\subsection{Blue Card}




The EU Blue Card is an alternative route, but not the primary plan.




It is more relevant if:




\begin{itemize}
\item a German/EU employer offers a qualifying salary;
\item the degree/qualification is accepted;
\item the role fits shortage or skilled-worker requirements;
\item relocation is planned.
\end{itemize}

English should remain the highest immediate language priority.




Short-term focus:




\begin{itemize}

\item technical explanations;

\item demo narration;

A formal English certificate is not urgent unless a visa, university or employer explicitly requests it.




\subsection{German}




German is not the highest ROI for the next 3–6 months if the goal is remote income from Colombia.




German becomes high ROI if:




\begin{itemize}
\item relocation to Germany becomes concrete;
\item marriage/residence route is activated;
\item local German employers become targets;
\item integration and bureaucracy become immediate.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{Portuguese}




Portuguese helps with:




\begin{itemize}
\item Portugal integration;
\item Brazil market;
\item bureaucracy;
\item social life;
\item future EU base.
\end{itemize}




It does not by itself create EU work authorization before the passport exists.




For Portugal, prioritize European Portuguese if relocation to Portugal is likely.

\section{9. Education and course strategy synthesis}




\subsection{Main principle}




Courses without certificates are still useful if they generate public evidence.




They are weak as credentials but useful as skill acquisition.




\subsection{Correct rule}




\begin{mdcode}
Bloque de codigo: text
Course value = output artifact, not course completion.
\end{mdcode}




\subsection{Short-term course policy}




During the first 90 days, courses must not displace:




\begin{itemize}
\item TwinSight case study;
\item portfolio MVP;
\item CV/LinkedIn/GitHub cleanup;
\item applications;
\item interviews.
\end{itemize}




\subsection{Rebelway}




Rebelway is valuable if used for:




\begin{itemize}
\item technical art specialization;
\item Houdini/procedural thinking;
\item VFX reel fragments;
\item real-time FX;
\item future technical artist differentiation.
\end{itemize}




It should not become the main short-term path unless the target shifts toward VFX/FX technical art.

\subsection{Master’s}




A master’s can be useful if it supports:




\begin{itemize}
\item EU relocation;
\item computer graphics;
\item simulation;
\item XR;
\item digital twins;
\item research/industry hybrid;
\item structured immigration.
\end{itemize}




It is not the fastest path to income.




\subsection{PhD}




A PhD should be avoided for now unless the target becomes research, academia, or advanced simulation/graphics R\&D.




For the current goal, it delays income and creates opportunity cost.

\section{11. TwinSight case study synthesis}




\subsection{Public positioning}

\item portfolio link.
\end{itemize}




C-priority applications should not consume deep customization time.

\section{15. Interview and negotiation synthesis}




\subsection{Preparation priorities}




Prepare hardest for:




\begin{enumerate}
\item explaining TwinSight;
\item Unity optimization;
\item WebGL constraints;
\item CAD-to-realtime pipeline;
\item C\# architecture;
\item technical UI;
\item AI-assisted development disclosure;
\item contractor availability;
\item salary expectations.
\end{enumerate}




\subsection{Take-home test policy}




Accept only if:




\begin{itemize}
\item scope is limited;
\item time requirement is reasonable;
\item no production work is being extracted;
\item ownership/IP terms are clear;
\item the company is legitimate;
\item the role is high enough priority.
\end{itemize}




Reject or renegotiate if:




\begin{itemize}
\item unpaid test exceeds reasonable scope;
\item it resembles client work;
\item it requires full feature delivery;
\item no feedback is promised;
\item company avoids contract clarity.
\end{itemize}




\subsection{Negotiation stance}




For contractor work:




\begin{mdcode}
Bloque de codigo: text
My expected range depends on scope, duration, time-zone overlap, and whether the role is contractor or employee. For international contractor work, I usually evaluate monthly retainers or hourly rates based on project complexity and expected availability.
\end{mdcode}




Do not reveal minimum too early.




\subsection{Offer scorecard}




Score offers on:




\begin{itemize}
\item gross compensation;
\item net compensation;
\item role fit;
\item portfolio leverage;
\item contract safety;
\item remote stability;
\item learning ROI;
\item EU leverage;
\item payment reliability;
\item IP and exclusivity terms.
\end{itemize}

\section{19. Final recommended strategy}




\subsection{Best path}




The best path is a \textbf{balanced but focused international contractor strategy}:




\begin{mdcode}
Bloque de codigo: text
Use TwinSight X500 as proof for Unity / Real-Time 3D / Technical Visualization roles.
Prioritize remote work from Colombia now.
Build toward EU employability through future Portuguese passport and possible Germany residence.
Use ARA and Python tooling only as secondary differentiation.
Avoid profile dilution.
\end{mdcode}




\subsection{Core execution sentence}




\begin{mdcode}
Bloque de codigo: text
For the next 90 days, every action must either strengthen TwinSight as proof, improve recruiter-facing credibility, create interview opportunities, or increase contractor readiness.
\end{mdcode}




\subsection{Final target profile}




\begin{mdcode}
Bloque de codigo: text
Real-Time 3D Developer / Unity Technical Artist with a focus on interactive technical visualization, CAD-to-realtime optimization, Unity WebGL deployment, and Python-assisted production tooling.
\end{mdcode}




\subsection{Final role targets}




\begin{enumerate}
\item Real-Time 3D / Interactive Technical Visualization Developer.
\item Unity WebGL / Interactive 3D Developer.
\item Technical Visualization / Digital Twin / Simulation Developer.
\item Unity Technical Artist focused on runtime, optimization and tooling.
\item Tools / Pipeline / Python Automation Developer as secondary path.
\end{enumerate}




\subsection{Final rule}




The first job does not need to be the final destination.




It must satisfy:




\begin{itemize}
\item compensation above the minimum threshold;
\item remote feasibility from Colombia;
\item defensible contract terms;
\item role fit with the real-time 3D direction;
\item ability to build toward USD 3k–6k/month;
\item no major strategic dilution.
\end{itemize}




If a role provides money but destroys positioning, treat it as a temporary cashflow decision, not as the main career strategy.
